tags.name: Drops Endpoints
tags.description:
Endpoints for discovering drops, checking mint eligibility, building mint transactions, and creating drops.

Creating an ERC-721 SeaDrop V1 drop, in the usual order:

1. POST /api/v2/drops/deploy with drop_type `seadrop_v1_erc721`, send the transaction, then poll GET /api/v2/drops/deploy/{chain}/{tx_hash}/receipt for the collection slug.
2. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug} to save the stages, max supply, and payout address as a draft. Allowlists for `signed_presale` stages are uploaded first with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/allowlist.
3. Items: POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media for upload contexts and upload each file, optionally upload a metadata manifest with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/manifest, then save them with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media/save-batch. Pass one upload_batch_id on every upload request for the set of files, then save that batch by filename.
4. Optionally, POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/prereveal-item to set the placeholder that every token shows until the reveal.
5. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/metadata/ipfs, polling GET /api/v2/drops/{slug}/metadata/ipfs/{workflow_execution_id} until it completes. This writes the real item metadata as the draft base URI.
6. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/publish, sending the transaction from the contract owner. The drop goes live once it is mined and indexed.
7. Minters use POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/mint.

Step 5 is the reveal. Run before the publish in step 6, the items are revealed as soon as the drop is live. To reveal later, publish without it, then run it and publish again when ready. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/unpublish returns a transaction that closes a live drop.

An ERC-1155 self-mint drop (drop_type `seadrop_v2_erc1155_self_mint`) skips steps 2 to 7. After deploying, get a media_token for each item's file from POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media and upload the file to the returned context. Each POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items with that token then returns a transaction that creates one token and mints its whole supply to the owner, and PUT /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/{token_id} returns one that updates an existing token's metadata.

quantity.description: Units of this NFT the account holds, in raw base units. Always 1 for ERC-721. Capped at 2147483647; read quantity_string for the exact value.

quantity_string.description: Exact units held, as a decimal string.

is_agent.description: Whether this account has declared itself an agent. Self-declared and not OpenSea verification, and the declaration on its own confers nothing: see GET /api/v2/accounts/{address_or_username}/agent-relationships for the ownership relationship, which is likewise a declaration rather than an authorization.

AgentMetadataResponse.description: The ERC-8004 registration file of an agent identity NFT, as parsed from its token URI. Self-reported by the agent's registrant and not verified by OpenSea.

active.description: Whether the agent declares itself active. ERC-8004 defaults this to true, so a registration file that omits it reads as true.

agent_wallet.description: The wallet the registration file names for the agent

fetched_at.description: When OpenSea last successfully read this registration file from the token URI, whether or not its content changed. A failed read does not advance it. Null when the file has not been read since OpenSea started recording this.

AgentRegistrationResponse.description: A registry entry an ERC-8004 registration file declares for the agent

AgentServiceResponse.description: A service endpoint declared in an ERC-8004 registration file

ChainIdentifier.description: Blockchain chain identifier. Use the chain slug (e.g., 'ethereum', 'polygon', 'arbitrum', 'optimism', 'base')

banner_image_url.description: Wide image for the collection, and the only wide image on this API. Use it for a header or hero slot; image_url is square and will not fill one. On the single-collection endpoint it is the collection's hero image, else its hero video's poster, else its banner; on list endpoints it is the banner. Always a still image: a video gets a frame from it, or null when no still can be derived.

image_url.description: Square avatar for the collection, used wherever it is named. Falls back to a representative item's image when the collection has none of its own.

banner_image_url.description: Wide image for the collection, and the only wide image on this API. Use it for a header or hero slot; image_url is square and will not fill one. On the single-collection endpoint it is the collection's hero image, else its hero video's poster, else its banner; on list endpoints it is the banner. Always a still image: a video gets a frame from it, or null when no still can be derived.

image_url.description: Square avatar for the collection, used wherever it is named. Falls back to a representative item's image when the collection has none of its own.

sales.description: Number of sales over the interval

volume.description: Trading volume over the interval, denominated in the currency named by volume_symbol

volume_symbol.description: Currency that volume is denominated in. Empty when the conversion rate was unavailable and the unit could not be determined.

order_hash.description: Seaport order hash, a 0x-prefixed 32-byte value. Absent on an order that settles through a Solana marketplace program, which has no Seaport identity and carries `svm_order` instead. Every EVM order has one.

price_per_item.description: Price of a single item in this order. For multi-quantity orders, `price` is the total for all items; divide by the item quantity or use this field for the per-item amount.

protocol.description: Marketplace protocol a Solana order settles through, which is what tells you which identity shape the order uses. Absent on a Seaport order, whose payload is unchanged. Only orders we can build fulfillment for carry a value here.

svm_order.description: Identity of a Solana order, present in place of `order_hash`. A client that assumes `order_hash` is always set should read this field first and fall back to `order_hash`.

current.description: What a buyer pays to fill this listing through OpenSea. For most listings this equals the sum of the consideration items in protocolData. A listing ingested from another marketplace may additionally include OpenSea's marketplace fee, which is applied to the transaction at fulfillment rather than being part of the order the seller signed; where that applies, the consideration in protocolData sums to less than this value.

order_hash.description: Seaport order hash, a 0x-prefixed 32-byte value. Absent on an order that settles through a Solana marketplace program, which has no Seaport identity and carries `svm_order` instead. Every EVM order has one.

price.description: Total consideration for the whole order (price per item multiplied by the order's item quantity). For a single-item order this equals `price_per_item`.

price_per_item.description: Price of a single item in this order. For multi-quantity orders, `price` is the total for all items; divide by the item quantity or use this field for the per-item amount.

protocol.description: Marketplace protocol a Solana order settles through, which is what tells you which identity shape the order uses. Absent on a Seaport order, whose payload is unchanged. Only orders we can build fulfillment for carry a value here.

svm_order.description: Identity of a Solana order, present in place of `order_hash`. A client that assumes `order_hash` is always set should read this field first and fall back to `order_hash`.

Price.description: An amount of a payment currency. `value` is expressed in the currency's base units (e.g. wei), i.e. the human-readable amount multiplied by 10^`decimals`.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, including fractional seconds

SvmOrderIdentity.description: Identity of an order that settles through a Solana marketplace program. Such an order has no Seaport order hash, so `order_hash` is absent from its payload and it is addressed instead by `id`, the transaction signature that created it joined to the onchain state account holding it. Pass that `id` wherever an endpoint takes an order hash.

asset_id.description: Mint of the asset the order is for, where the program records one. Absent otherwise.

creation_signature.description: Signature of the transaction that created the order. The first half of `id`.

id.description: `creation_signature:order_state`. This is what an endpoint expecting an order hash takes for a Solana order, for example `GET /api/v2/orders/chain/solana/protocol/{protocol_address}/{order_hash}`. Base58 and case-sensitive; do not lowercase it.

order_state.description: Address of the onchain account holding the order's state. The second half of `id`.

floor_price.description: Price of the cheapest current listing, denominated in the currency named by floor_price_symbol. 0 when the collection has no listing.

floor_price_symbol.description: Currency that floor_price is denominated in. Empty when there is no listing.

num_owners.description: Number of distinct addresses holding an item in the collection

volume.description: All-time trading volume, denominated in the currency named by volume_symbol. This is not necessarily the currency of floor_price.

volume_symbol.description: Currency that volume is denominated in. Empty when the conversion rate was unavailable and the unit could not be determined.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, on the errors that have one. Branch on it rather than on the message text, which may change.

WalletAuth.description: OpenSea wallet authorization. Run `opensea login` or use the OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow with PKCE, then send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

BadRequest.description: For error reasons, review the response data.

Forbidden.description: Wallet token lacks permission for this request

InternalError.description: Internal server error. Please open a support ticket so OpenSea can investigate.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Maximum requests per rate limit window

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with 429 rate-limit responses and with 503 responses the request can be retried after.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix epoch timestamp when the rate limit window resets
